findings.body: The raw-stream cases assert the latest visible step, but never assert the ten-second retention bound. With FORGE_NOW frozen, replacing coalescing with an append for every notification would still satisfy these assertions and the final twenty-event check, which excludes progress records. This leaves an explicit detail-7 recording rule untested. Extend the command-level stream test to verify that a burst retains one progress record while exposing its latest step. This concerns proof of the accepted coalescing ruling, not changing that ruling.

findings.body: Claude can report a missing resumed session as an error result on stdout ([upstream reproduction](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/40609)). This decoder prefixes its errors with `error_during_execution`, so the worker's existing prefix check at src/forge/worker.py:443–445 no longer recognizes that result. The reader likewise checks only stderr at src/forge/story.py:738–740, although decoded result errors are returned on stdout. For a structured-only missing-session failure, both paths refuse instead of starting the intended fresh session. Preserve structured error information for recovery in both callers; the existing stub's plain stderr error does not exercise this case.
findings.title: Preserve missing-session recovery for structured Claude errors

findings.body: The previous P2 remains unresolved. Both views read events.jsonl without the writer guard at src/forge/board.py:203–204. On Windows, an overlapping reader can make this replacement raise PermissionError, aborting progress reporting and its enclosing worker, reader, review or test command. The guard serializes writers only. Use bounded reader-lock retries, as the existing replacement helper does at src/forge/codex.py:532–539.
findings.title: Handle Windows readers holding the progress file open
